Title: Diagnosis of test `testGenerateURLFragment`
Details: The test `testGenerateURLFragment` checks whether HTML entities such as `"` are correctly escaped to their corresponding character by the `StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment` method. However, the test failure indicates that this is not the case. Following the execution path, we find that `StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment` is not escaping any HTML code; instead, it is using its input `toolTipText` as is. Consequently, un-escaped strings are being returned, which leads to the error demonstrated by the test.

Title: Diagnosis of test `testDefaultArgName`

Details:
The test `testDefaultArgName` creates an Option with `OptionBuilder.hasArg().isRequired().create("f")` which sets the option to require an argument, and it creates a single Option "f" that is required. Then the test creates a `HelpFormatter` and sets its argument name by calling `formatter.setArgName("argument")`, expecting that this default argument name is used in the usage output for options missing explicit argument names.

From the investigation of the `HelpFormatter.printUsage` method, it collects all options and for each non-grouped option calls `appendOption` on a buffer that accumulates usage syntax. The `appendOption` code confirms the option syntax text appends the option character and also appends the argument in the form `<argName>` if the option has an argument and has a non-empty argument name (checked by `option.hasArgName()`).

Looking at the `Option.hasArgName()` method, it simply checks if the option's internal `argName` string is not null and not empty. The `Option.getArgName()` returns this internal `argName`.

The key detail is seen in `OptionBuilder.create(String)`: when creating an option, it sets `option.setArgName(argName)` where this `argName` is the static `OptionBuilder.argName`, which is the argument name set on the builder, not the `HelpFormatter.defaultArgName`. Also, the `HelpFormatter.setArgName` method only sets the `defaultArgName` field on `HelpFormatter`. 

Since `OptionBuilder` static state for `argName` is never set in the test, the option is created with a null or empty argument name. Therefore, in `appendOption`, the condition `option.hasArgName()` is false and `<argument>` is never appended. This explains why the usage string doesn't contain `<argument>` for the option and the test fails.

In short, the test expects `HelpFormatter` to use its default argument name for options missing explicit argument names, but the option instance itself never gets that default argument name value. The current implementation only uses the option's own argument name to print usage, ignoring `HelpFormatter`'s default arg name.

Suggested fix is to modify `HelpFormatter.appendOption` to use the `HelpFormatter.defaultArgName` when `option.hasArgName()` is false and the option expects an argument.

Suggested locations to fix:
org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.appendOption(java.lang.StringBuffer,org.apache.commons.cli.Option,boolean)
org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.printUsage(java.io.PrintWriter,int,java.lang.String,org.apache.commons.cli.Options)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
